Holy shit, there are some really terrible responses here.

Start off - "Don't let school interfere with your education" - Mark Twain.

I didn't get straight A's. The most successful people don't get straight A's. Straight A's are what you fall back on if you have nothing else going for you.

"Making it through" - This is such a pessimistic way to look at university. You don't want to make it through, you should want to excel. Figure out what you enjoy and make sure you always have time for that. Clubs are designed so that you can (hopefully) find people who share your interests.

The first tip I have to "making it through" is to put everything in perspective.

The best way to find perspective, is to make time for what you actually enjoy.
I do enjoy university, I'm finally studying things that I actually want to. However, that doesn't mean it isn't hard.

I think, as a university senior, the biggest thing to learn is that learning your major is maybe 50% of why you are there. The other 50% is learning how to learn. I know that sounds weird, but learning how to learn is important. University, early on especially, will help you develop a lot of the skills you need to learn to continue to be a lifelong learner. How to learn effectively, how to gather important information, how to take good notes, and important skills like that. Do not neglect these things.

The best way to nurture that growth in learning is to take advantage early on and take good notes. Reread your notes later. Take an hour out of your day and reread your notes for the week, study them and go over them, underline or circle anything you don't totally understand, and ask your professors in their office hours. If you don't understand something after class, go talk to your professor during office hours. Use the office hours, they are a very handy tool.

In short, the biggest advice I have is to take advantage of the tools at your disposal and become a good learner.

Another tip, don't let your life get to you too much. At times, you may feel stressed out by school, by work, by everything. Take a load off occasionally. I'm not saying go party every Friday night or go out every weekend, but I am saying to give yourself adequate time to relax and refresh. If you burn the candle at both ends, you're just going to burn out faster. Burnout 3 weeks before finals week is NOT fun.

get a planner and write due date and set goals for what work you will get done and what days. Don't be afraid to take breaks but don't get carried away.

Don't study everyday for a class, instead take a day of break from that class and review the material the next day. This will help you memorize things better.

Sleep! No matter how much work you have, it's useless to study when you are tired.

Don't miss class. If you miss class, don't be surprised to see your grade go down. Even if you get notes from someone else, it's not the same. Good note takers are also hard to find. Also when you don't understand something, ask questions. This will help you understand the subject better, stand out to the professor and if your grades are good, you have a good recommendation letter coming your way.
Take advantage of support services offered. Is there a peer tutor group or writing lab on campus? Check it out once you have a course syllabus to see if they would be a helpful resource.
